script: [serious] The CIA tried to turn a cat into a spy. In the 1960s, the agency put a microphone in a cat's ear, a transmitter at the base of its skull, and an antenna woven through its fur. The plan: let the cat wander near targets and listen. The project was called Acoustic Kitty, and by one estimate it cost about twenty million dollars. One famous account says the first cat was hit by a taxi on its first mission. That story is disputed. What isn't: in 1967, the CIA gave up. A cat, it turned out, does whatever it wants. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number nineteen. A new file every day.
